results.title: interest rates essay (Maxim)
results.known: 24–25 out of 25, per the examiner (a real confirmed range, not a single invented number — deliberately kept as a range here rather than forced to one figure).

issues.text: interest rates only increae the cost of borrowing, does not therefore reduced dispoable incomes of consumers.

results.improvement: Add a brief explanation that higher rates reduce disposable income by increasing borrowing costs, which can reduce consumption.

results.title: monopoly efficiency essay (Seb)
results.known: 21 out of 25, marked by his teacher (confirmed with George 2026-08-12 — not Seb's own self-assessment, which was the thing worth ruling out given Seb's interview describes him self-marking).

issues.text: Misuses the concept of SNP and X‑inefficiency, writing 'SNP (P−C×Q)' and 'X‑inefficient (produce even AC and still make SNP)' which confuses the cost structure and indicates a misunderstanding of monopoly inefficiency.
Uses the term 'satisfice' without definition and in a confusing way, weakening the clarity of the argument.

results.improvement: Clarify the sentence 'Thames Water are therefore price makers and can afford to satisfice or be X‑inefficient (produce even AC and still make SNP (P−C×Q))' by explaining that a monopoly can produce at a higher average cost than the minimum efficient scale, earning surplus without minimising costs, rather than using the confusing phrase.

results.title: carbon emissions / road traffic essay
results.known: 22 out of 25. Marker not yet specified — confirm whether this was a teacher or an examiner before treating it as a firm anchor (same standard applied to Test 2).

issues.text: The claim that ‘MPC=MSC, thus shifting behaviour to switch (MPC + tax) fully internalising the DWL and eliminating market failure’ is inaccurate – a tax shifts MPC up to MSC but may not eliminate DWL.

results.improvement: Clarify the sentence ‘MPC=MSC, thus shifting behaviour to switch (MPC + tax) fully internalising the DWL and eliminating market failure’ by explaining that the tax shifts the marginal private cost curve upward, reducing quantity and price, but may not fully internalise the DWL; the DWL is reduced but not eliminated.

results.title: National Minimum Wage / social care essay
results.known: 19–20 out of 25, marked by the teacher (confirmed with George 2026-08-13). Originally reported only as "mid A", which is a grade band rather than a mark — the real figure was obtained rather than inferred from a grade boundary, since guessing it and then treating the guess as ground truth is exactly the substitution this project exists to prevent. Kept as a range, which is honest, rather than forced to one number.

issues.text: social care firms are unable to produce at socially optimum level (Pt Qt) and instead just produce at (PQ) where MPC is less than MSC.
S=MPC and MSC, MSC below MPC.
increase in national living wage may not have a significant impact on the firm's costs.

results.improvement: Clarify that for a positive externality the MSC should lie above the MPC, not below, and explain how this shifts the socially optimal quantity.

results.title: globalisation essay (Luke)
